title: Projected q-Shells for Nested Gausslet Bases
abstract: Electronic-structure calculations require a finite representation of both the electronic wave functions and their Coulomb interaction. Conventional compact basis sets lead to a four-index interaction. Gausslet basis sets are one of a very small number of approaches that allow a much smaller two-index interaction, similar to a real-space grid, but with far fewer points. The continuing challenge in their development is reducing further the number of functions needed while maintaining high accuracy. Here we introduce projected q-shells (PQS), an improvement to the nested Cartesian gausslets of White and Lindsey. Their standard nesting construction divides a joining shell into disjoint faces, edges, and corners, reducing its polynomial completeness from order q to order q-2. PQS approximately restores the two lost orders. In terms of completeness, we prove that for an ideal, undistorted parent, the span of the PQS basis is equivalent to an overcomplete basis of overlapping patches. Coordinate distortions, which are always used in practice, harm this equivalence only slightly. The moment properties that allow two-index interactions also become inexact, even without distortion, but we show that the improvement in order more than makes up for this loss. For similar basis sizes, PQS gives smaller one-electron and interaction errors on small molecules, such as H2+, H2, and C2, than standard nesting. The improvement is largest for more compact bases with smaller q.
summary: This paper introduces Projected q-Shells (PQS), an advanced basis set technique designed to improve upon existing methods for electronic structure calculations. PQS enhances the accuracy and completeness of the basis set representation by mathematically restoring lost polynomial orders during the basis contraction process. This results in more accurate and efficient calculations for molecular electronic properties.
main_problem: Electronic-structure calculations require accurately representing both electronic wave functions and the Coulomb interaction using a finite basis set representation.
main_result: Projected q-Shells (PQS) offer an improvement over standard nested Gausslet constructions by approximately restoring the lost polynomial completeness order, leading to smaller computational errors for small molecules.
method: The authors introduce PQS, an advanced basis set construction that improves upon nested Cartesian gausslets by using a projection technique to maintain high local polynomial completeness while keeping the interaction manageable.
model_or_system: The method is applied to electronic structure calculations for atoms and molecules (e.g., H2+, H2, C2), focusing on approximating the computationally expensive four-index Coulomb interaction with a two-index form.
key_observables: One-electron and interaction errors; polynomial completeness order ($q$ vs $q-2$); mean Cartesian rms width ($\sigma^2$) and relative center shift ($d_{12}$).
important_parameters: The basis set parameter $q$ (related to polynomial order) and the degree of coordinate distortion.
main_assumptions: The ideal model assumes undistorted parent lattices; practical use involves coordinate distortions, which slightly compromise the theoretical equivalence.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates four methods of spatial resolution change, including PQS compression. Figure 2 compares WL nesting (disjoint pieces) versus PQS (full contraction $ightarrow$ projection $ightarrow$ reorthogonalization) in 2D.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of basis set representation, details the limitations of standard nesting, mathematically derives the PQS construction via the projected-shell theorem, and validates the method by comparing PQS results against standard nesting for small molecules.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum chemistry, the core mathematical machinery—developing highly accurate, compact, and systematically improvable basis sets for electron-electron interactions—is crucial for any simulation involving many-body quantum systems, including those studied in AMO physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Four ways of changing spatial resolution. (a) Adaptive multiwavelet blocks. (b) Wavelet multiresolution. (c) Over- lapping full gausslet patches at several scales. (d) Projected q-shell compression of the same patches. The dashed interior functions in (d) are removed because their space is already supplied by the finer patch.

FIG. 2. Parent lattice and two-dimensional q = 5 shell. (a) A distorted parent lattice, the uncontracted central block, and one surrounding shell. (b) WL treats the corners and the four three-function sides separately. (c) PQS starts from the complete 5 × 5 local block. Its 16 products having at least one edge factor are projected onto the shell of parent-lattice sites shown in (a) and then reorthogonalized; the nine middle– middle products are omitted. Panels (b) and (c) have the same number of functions but retain different local polynomial information.

FIG. 4. Projected full-configuration-interaction (FCI) errors for H2 with the same H/cc-pV6Z s, p residual-Gaussian supple- ment. At each geometry, every lower-order FCI wave function is projected into the same supplemented PQS ns = 7 basis and its energy is evaluated with the ns = 7 Hamiltonian. The plotted error is this energy minus the FCI complete-basis-set (CBS) limit of Pachucki. Colors and symbols denote ns as in Fig. 3; solid filled symbols denote PQS and dashed open sym- bols WL. The source dimensions are equal at each geometry and order.

FIG. 3. Restricted-HF comparison for H2 supplemented by contracted Cartesian H/cc-pV6Z s and p residual Gaussians, at equal PQS and WL dimensions. All three panels plot error magnitudes. Panel (a) compares the IDA Coulomb energy with the parent-basis value for the same converged orbital. Panel (b) uses the RHF energy obtained with the IDA Hamiltonian; panel (c) reevaluates the same orbital with the common parent Hamiltonian. The reference for (b) and (c) is the HF basis-set limit estimated from Cartesian aug-cc-pV5Z and aug-cc-pV6Z. Solid filled symbols denote PQS and dashed open symbols WL.

FIG. 5. Numerical realization for an undistorted, unit-spaced parent chain, an outer segment with R = 4, and q = 5. The nine parent gausslets are gray. (a) The five outer-patch COMX functions (blue) and five inner-patch functions (red). (b) The original outer edge functions (dashed) and their projections onto the two endpoint parent gausslets forming the parent- lattice shell (solid), together with the inner-patch functions. The complete-patch union and the projected construction both have rank seven, and their projector residual is 1.12 × 10−15, illustrating Eq. (A17). Vertical offsets are for clarity.
